First reasoned review, 2026-10-23

Verdicts and execution paths

* `9574.tgz` (SHA-256 5bd24fa5dd2f27b9ac45f2c9e6cfa61a1de0e324b8435162c7937736e905418a): MALICIOUS. This is spender's public The Rebel CVE-2009-2698 local kernel exploit, identified by its source and corroborated by https://www.exploit-db.com/exploits/9574. `therebel.sh` compiles and invokes the exploit, choosing executable or PulseAudio shared-module paths based on mmap_min_addr and SELinux. `pwnkernel.c` sets PER_SVR4, checks root-owned SUID PulseAudio, and uses its `-L` module option. `exploit.c` maps page zero, places kernel callbacks into a forged dst_entry, and triggers udp_sendmsg using MSG_PROXY|MSG_MORE followed by sendto. The kernel callback clears audit/AppArmor/SELinux controls, resets security_ops when applicable, clears CR0.WP to patch sel_read_enforce to report enforcement, and installs root credentials (or zeroes task UID/GID fields). It then launches `/bin/sh -i`. Public research provenance is a plausible legitimate explanation for possession; the active escalation and deceptive security-state patching tip the machine-triage verdict. No authorized testing context or evidence of execution is supplied. This is not evidence of a trojanized upstream artifact.
* `python-webhook-site-env-exfil.py` (SHA-256 9cb13475bdf5e7320dd19e79bf72e9bc1a897c72c83c58197db7c67bd7d73be1): MALICIOUS. At module load it snapshots every process environment variable, JSON-serializes and UTF-8 encodes the snapshot, puts it into a POST Request to a fixed webhook.site UUID, sets Content-Type, and opens that exact Request. There is no filtering or consent gate. An intentional collector test is possible but undocumented. Secret presence and successful delivery are unknown; the complete source-to-send path is concrete. Only one distinct hostile behavior is supported, so the one-hostile coverage gap is intentional; no duplicate or invented theft behavior was added.
* `dev-tcp-alternate-test.sh` (SHA-256 d3c7ae8a6626cb5e4e64f16e7e7f5bb58c8550ef552ceeceb9fb9df4ac609c75): MALICIOUS. Running it immediately starts interactive Bash, opens an outbound TCP connection to 10.0.0.1:4444, redirects stdout/stderr to that socket with `&>`, and duplicates that socket descriptor onto stdin with `0>&1`. No wrapper makes the command inert. A private destination and a test-like filename establish neither authorization nor isolation. Endpoint ownership and actual reachability are unknown. The two existing hostile rules describe the same reverse-shell behavior; both remain accurate and are preserved, without inventing a second distinct objective.

No sample was executed. All source was read, including all three archive members; atomscan and cleave facts were run on each original. There is no obfuscation or concealed payload in these source files. The Python flow graph has a general source-local reachability limitation, and atomscan records flow-field-unavailable/flow-query-incomplete; direct source tracing still establishes the Request/body/urlopen chain. No fetched dependencies contributed findings.

Corrections and preserved coverage

Six old IDs were relocated with their matchers and exclusions retained. No accurate behavior was deleted. Exact and ancestor directory consumers were audited; there are no ancestor selectors for the moved source leaves, and all exact and local consumers were updated.

* CR0 inline assembly is now a notable kernel-register operation, not evidence of hooking or a rootkit by itself. The complemented WP mask remains suspicious in that neutral home, with a name and description limited to its actual expression matcher.
* commit_creds and the nearby prepare_kernel_cred pair are kernel-credential references, not proof of a module or escalation. The pair is now notable. Kernel credential API/task-flag references likewise no longer claim a kill hook.
* The SUID composite establishes a mode check near execution; it does not bind the checked file to the launched path or establish exploitation. It is now notable under file stat, and its attack composites still reference it. The unrelated-exec fixture demonstrates that unsupported inference.
* New suspicious AST assignment matchers detect audit disabling, AppArmor disabling, AppArmor audit disabling, and LSM operations reset. They reject comments, strings, reads, declarations, writes enabling the controls, and clearing a pointer rather than its pointee. Zero spelling variants are tested.
* New notable traits cover fixed address-zero mmap requests and personality source calls. Neither capability alone convicts an exploit.

The original root-shell and deceptive SELinux hostile findings remain. The Python and reverse-shell findings are unchanged. Original archive summary: 2 hostile, 6 suspicious, 35 notable. Final: 2 hostile, 7 suspicious, 40 notable. exploit.c: 2H/5S/17N -> 2H/7S/21N; pwnkernel.c: 0H/1S/4N -> 0H/0S/6N; therebel.sh unchanged at 15N. The loss of pwnkernel.c's suspicious classification is the intentional correction of the unbound SUID inference, not loss of its supported checks/execution.

Model disagreement

`scan-comparison.json` records all before/after IDs, criticalities, risks, model heads, and archive members. The installed model is v18.18 and warns that its feature spec is older than the extractor (18 versus 19). Scan-time full rule validation was disabled using CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0 because the old atomscan engine rejects the already-documented 101-rule metadata/file/naming budget; no rules were altered to accommodate that engine. The independent final make validation uses the newer cleave engine.

Before: archive aggregate probability 0.9933702, level 1, primary model head class 2; Python 0.96025026, level -1, model heads class 0; Bash 0.93795335, level -1, model heads class 0. After: archive probability 0.98, level 25, model heads class 0; both small scripts unchanged. Thus the model heads miss the supported attacks (including the archive after correcting neutral evidence), despite retained hostile static findings. The outer archive still receives level 25 in the combined report. Live terminal verdicts after edits are HOSTILE[92%] for the archive, BENIGN[48%] for Python, and BENIGN[47%] for Bash; the two script verdicts directly disagree with their supported hostile static findings. Do not restore incorrect objective placement or duplicate rules to influence those scores.

Fixtures and provenance

`exploit.c`, `pwnkernel.c`, and `therebel.sh` are verbatim copies from the supplied archive. `environment-export.py` and `reverse-shell.sh` are byte-identical copies of the supplied scripts under stable fixture names.

`full-nelson.c` is a separate real public exploit fetched with forager from https://www.exploit-db.com/raw/15704. Its root callback calls commit_creds(prepare_kernel_cred(0)); a separate path obtains kernel execution through Econet and launches a shell without `-i`. Before/after checks retain its credential references and pairing. It did not have a hostile kernel-root-credentials-interactive-shell match before (it requests no interactive flag), and the move introduces no such claim. `linux-cred.c` is the real Linux v6.12 kernel/cred.c fetched with forager from https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/plain/kernel/cred.c?h=v6.12. It implements ordinary kernel credential handling and demonstrates why bare APIs do not establish an exploit. Original artifacts and their .forage.json provenance remain in session scratch.

Other C fixtures are synthetic controls. They supplement the supplied exploit, the independently fetched Full Nelson attack, and the real kernel source; they are not used to erase any attack technique. Run `python3 testdata/triage/therebel-env-devtcp-first-review/check.py` for the ten static focused checks. If using cleave and atomscan builds with different YARA serialization versions, give cleave its own CLEAVE_CACHE_DIR to avoid sharing incompatible compiled cache files. The sources are never compiled or run.
